experiment.name: Habitus grade against distance from the Beagle reference course in natural B. rossi infection (DS05)
experiment.description: Is admission severity in natural B. rossi infection partly the stage a dog has reached on a common course, and are the worst dogs off that course? Habitus grade in DS05 is tested against distance from a course built from 5 experimentally infected Beagles, controlling position along it.

experiment.summary: Exploratory (DS05 already seen). Habitus against distance from the Beagle course, controlling pseudo-stage: partial rho -0.24 (95% CI -0.39 to -0.07), p 0.005, n 147 dogs; it vanishes once haematocrit is also controlled (partial rho 0.08). results.title: Position on the map by habitus grade (DS05)

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Is part of the variation in admission severity of natural B. rossi infection the stage a dog has reached on a common course, and are the clinically worst dogs off that course rather than only later on it?

The reference course comes from 5 experimentally infected Beagles (DS02, SRC-B) in the plane haematocrit by log reticulocytes. Severity is the habitus grade of DS05 (SRC-F, 147 B. rossi dogs; 4 bright to 0 collapsed). DS05 was examined before this plan, so every result here is exploratory.

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: A principal curve (cubic in arc length) was fitted to the 22 pre-treatment Beagle samples, as spec.md fixed. Each DS05 dog was projected onto it: pseudo-stage is the position along the curve (0 to 1) and distance is the gap to the curve in units of the Beagles' own scatter (0.37 SD units). The primary test is the partial Spearman correlation of habitus with distance, controlling pseudo-stage (10,000 Freedman-Lane permutations, 2,000 bootstrap resamples of dogs, seed 20261112).

Deviation D1: the spec fit did not converge (100 iterations) and re-ordered the Beagle samples, so its pseudo-stage barely follows the sampling day (rho 0.19). A time-anchored course (the curve parameter kept at the sampling day) keeps the order better (rho 0.58). Its results are shown beside the spec results as a sensitivity; the spec results stay primary because the deviation was chosen after outcome numbers had been printed.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: Primary (spec construction): partial rho -0.24 (95% CI -0.39 to -0.07), permutation p 0.005, BH q 0.007, n 147. Dogs further from the course had a duller habitus. Controlling haematocrit as well (S3) removes it: partial rho 0.08 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.24). Distance largely restates anaemia, which was already known to track habitus (rho 0.53).
Pseudo-stage with habitus (H2): rho 0.29 (95% CI 0.13 to 0.42). Band-neutrophil plane (H3): partial rho -0.12 (95% CI -0.28 to 0.06), q 0.150.

Geometry: 61% of DS05 dogs project onto an end of the Beagle course and only 24% lie within 2 spread units of it. The pre-treatment Beagles span haematocrit 0.12 to 0.42; the median DS05 dog has 0.18.

Time-anchored course (D1): 54% of dogs lie past its late end; the illness-duration check fails (rho -0.21, opposite to the prediction); habitus with distance given stage: partial rho -0.54 (95% CI -0.67 to -0.40), -0.29 with haematocrit also controlled.
Leaving one Beagle out changes the curve a lot: under the spec construction the rank agreement of pseudo-stage with the full fit ranges from -0.74 to 0.92.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: It does not show that severe dogs are "late" or "off course": the stage score is not validated under either construction, and most natural dogs are more anaemic than any Beagle before treatment, so the 5-dog course cannot place them.
Distance from the course is mostly a restatement of anaemia. Off-course dogs are not a subtype. No prediction is made.
Single species and country; prior treatment unknown; the Beagle course follows intravenous inoculation. DS05 has no hard outcome; habitus is a proxy.
